document.title: Zoo Project File SoftSpec
document.purpose: Describe the canonical structure and operational role of zoo-project.json as currently authored and maintained by zookeep.
author: Lion Kimbro
Codex

overview.basic: zoo-project.json records a project's identity, repository identity, repository kind, licensing preference, hosting preference, and repo-type-specific metadata. Python distribution names and import-package names are separate concepts and are recorded separately.
character: Advisory data for zookeep and related tools rather than a rigid validation boundary.
Extensible: tools should preserve unfamiliar keys when rewriting the file.
overview.presence: The file is optional for general repository operation. Commands that create, inspect, repair, set up, or publish a zookeep project may require it or behave differently when it is absent.

historical-source: The output structure defined by zookeep.init-and-doctor.spec.v1.
The legacy python-package addition defined by zookeep.setup-and-python-package.spec.v1.
format-basis.canonical-source: The current zookeep spec and doctor implementation.
format-basis.legacy-migration: Older zoo-project.json files may omit zookeep-project-guid or use python-package.name. Doctor adds a generated GUID when needed, obtains the Python distribution name from pyproject.toml when possible, obtains an import-package name from the legacy field or an unambiguous src/ directory, writes the explicit python structure, and removes python-package.
difference-from-v1: Adds the canonical zookeep-project-guid field and its first-key ordering rule.
Replaces the ambiguous python-package structure with separate Python distribution and import-package identities.
Describes fields authored by current spec as required in canonical output.
Does not include project-ref because current project specs, implementation, and authored files do not use it.
Corrects the project-name description: current code requires a non-empty value but does not enforce the v1 acceptance-regex.
Uses the SoftSpec v3 wrapper, schema definition, object keys, constraints, vocabulary, and data-dictionary forms.

spec-editor.new-file-behavior: Open a tkinter form and create zoo-project.json from the entered values.
spec-editor.existing-file-behavior: Open the same form with current values prefilled, then update the fields represented by the form.
preservation: Preserve unknown top-level and nested extension fields.
Edit the primary Python import-package entry and preserve additional import-package entries.

pyproject-reconciliation.existing-file-behavior: Parse pyproject.toml while preserving formatting, comments, and unrelated values. Change only project.name when it differs from python.distribution.name.
pyproject-reconciliation.missing-file-behavior: Create a minimal setuptools pyproject.toml using src-layout discovery, project.name from python.distribution.name, version 0.1.0, and requires-python >=3.10.
pyproject-reconciliation.boundary: Import-package names are represented by python.import-packages and their source paths. They are not inferred from or written to project.name.

uuid4-string.description: A UUID version 4 serialized as a string.

repository-type.description: A repository breed identifier used to select light repo-type-specific behavior.

vocabulary.python-2026-03: A Python repository using the March 2026 project conventions.
vocabulary.philosophy-discussion-2026-03: A discussion-oriented repository using the March 2026 project conventions.

notes: Current spec accepts any non-empty string and does not validate this value against the vocabulary.
Only python-2026-03 currently triggers repo-type-specific package setup behavior.

repository-visibility.description: Preferred visibility when creating a hosted repository.

python-distribution-name.description: The Python distribution name used by package indexes and commands such as pip install.

python-import-package-name.description: A name used in a Python import statement. It may differ from the distribution and repository names.

project-relative-path.description: A forward-slash path relative to the project repository root.

zoo-project-file.title: zoo-project.json
zoo-project-file.description: Canonical current content of a zoo-project.json file.
rules: zookeep-project-guid is serialized as the first top-level key.
Current spec authors every unconditional required field in this schema.
python should be present when repo-type is python-2026-03.
python.distribution.name is the distribution identity used by pip and pyproject.toml project.name.
Each python.import-packages entry identifies an import name independently of the distribution and repository names.
Unknown top-level and nested keys are allowed and should be preserved by tools that rewrite the file.
Existing values are advisory unless a command documents a stronger precondition.

zookeep-project-guid.description: Stable zookeep identity for this project. Generated by init or added by doctor if absent.

created_by: zookeep doctor when the key is absent
data-dictionary.used_for: Identify the project independently of its directory or repository name.

repo-type.description: Repository breed used to select light convention-specific behavior.

license.description: Preferred license identifier used by tools that generate a LICENSE file.

repository.description: Preferences for repository hosting and publication.

visibility.description: Preferred visibility for a newly published repository.

python.description: Explicit Python distribution and import-package identities.

name.description: Name used by pip install and pyproject.toml project.name.

import-packages.description: Python packages provided for import by the distribution. A distribution may provide more than one.

name.description: Name used in an import statement.

path.description: Repository-relative directory containing the import package.

created_by: zookeep doctor while migrating legacy Python metadata
data-dictionary.used_for: Reconcile pyproject.toml and locate or create import-package directories.
